pending.subject: Show a prompt's unended line while the command waits (#1723)
pending.body:
* Show a prompt's unended line while the command waits

A prompt or a picker's last line ends without a newline and is followed by a
wait, so the drain loop never got the later read that would flush it. Poll
the pty while text is held and flush it once the pty has been quiet for
flushInterval.

Refs #1722

* Retry an interrupted poll and skip it for a lone partial character

poll() returning EINTR fell through to a blocking read, so a held prompt
could stay hidden until more output came. A held tail that is only the start
of a multi-byte character has nothing to show, so it no longer arms the idle
flush; the read waits for the rest of it.

Adds cases for a character split across reads, colour escapes, carriage-return
progress frames, large output, and Stop while a prompt is held.

* Keep a truncated character's bytes instead of dropping them

A command that exits partway through a multi-byte character left its lead
bytes in the decoder, and the exit flush stopped short of them, so they were
silently lost. They are now shown as they are once nothing can complete them.

0xF5 and up never begin a UTF-8 character (RFC 3629), so they are no longer
held back waiting for continuation bytes that cannot make them valid.

* Stop the held-prompt test once the prompt shows, not on a timer

A fixed 300 ms stop could land before a slow shell start printed the prompt, failing the case under load even though prompt flushing works.

pending.subject: fix(extensions): opt URLSession out of the macOS AppSSO broker (#1739)
pending.body:
* fix(extensions): opt URLSession out of the macOS AppSSO broker

On macOS, URLSession hands a request to any installed Extensible SSO
 (AppSSO) extension whose identity-provider URLs it matches, such as an enterprise SSO broker. An extension does plain HTTP and sets its own cookies and headers; when
 a server answers a redirect to one of those IdP URLs, the broker intercepts it and, with no window or interactive context behind a launcher's background fetch, fails
 the request with com.apple.AppSSO.AuthorizationError -5. Disable the broker for the extension fetcher's URLSession via the same process-wide private class method
 WebKit uses for its own non-interactive loads, behind a responds(to:) check so it is a no-op where unavailable.

* Scope extension AppSSO opt-out to its session

Deeplinks: input, ask-once consent and a Debug scheme for built-in commands (#1753)
pending.body:
* Add deeplinks for built-in launcher commands

Every row that can take a hotkey now runs by URL: tinycast://<kind>/<id>
for the row ID <kind>:<id>, such as tinycast://command/clipboard-history.
The link resolves to the same HotKeyAction a shortcut fires, so it toggles,
respects feature switches, and works before the index is built. Copy
Deeplink (⇧⌘C, or ⌘K on the row) copies the link, extension rows included.

* Give deeplinks input, consent and a channel scheme

Built on Rohith's tinycast://<kind>/<id> links, now with the rest of what
a Raycast deeplink can do, for Tinycast's own commands only:

- Input in Raycast's names: fallbackText types into a command's first
  field, arguments (JSON object or array) fill quicklink and custom
  command fields, and context (or launchContext) fills the create
  editors. Malformed or oversized input refuses the link.
- tinycast://search?fallbackText= and tinycast://settings/<tab>.
- create-quicklink and create-snippet open a filled-in editor that saves
  nothing until Save; create-note starts the note with the text.
- A link from outside that acts outside Tinycast asks once: Always Allow,
  Run Once or Cancel. Screens never ask. Always Allow is listed in
  Settings > General > Deeplinks, and never travels in a backup.
- A quicklink whose link is our own scheme runs in-process, unasked.
- Debug answers tinycast-dev://, so a local build never takes the
  installed app's links.
- A plain `open` no longer makes window commands act on Tinycast: when
  Tinycast is frontmost, the menu-bar owner is the target.
- Extension links stay on their own path: the built-in router never
  touches extension types, and the launcher asks ExtensionCoordinator
  for an extension row's link.

* Describe deeplinks on their own terms, and stop quicklink loops

A quicklink's own-scheme link runs in-process and synchronously, so one
that reached a quicklink could reach itself and recurse forever; it is
now refused with a HUD. Drops the input aliases that only mirrored
another app's payloads.

* Add note, chat, batch, volume and window-size links; ask before input

New links for features Tinycast already has:
- tinycast://note/<file> and tinycast://chat/<uuid> open that note or
  saved chat; the note switcher and the chat menus copy their links.
- command/ai-chat-window?fallbackText= adds text to the unsent line.
- create-quicklink and create-snippet take a context list, added only
  after the reader agrees, duplicates skipped.
- system-action/set-volume takes a 0-100 level and skips the picker.
- window-size?arguments={width,height,anchor,x,y} sizes the front window.
- Copy Deeplink carries the values typed into a row's fields, and every
  Settings shortcut field offers it on right-click.
- Create Snippet starts from the selected text, read through
  Accessibility, never with Cmd-C.

From review:
- Any link from outside that carries input now asks, shows the input,
  and Always Allow remembers only that exact input. Typed text was one
  Return from a fallback row such as Run Shell Command.
- The question defaults to Cancel; a missing target is reported before
  anything is asked.
- The input cap counts UTF-8 bytes, not characters.
- createNote() keeps its no-argument form, which NotesView needs.
- A link that launches the app waits until start() has wired handlers.
- The palette records the app a link-opened palette covered.
- Extension links use the running channel's scheme.

* Ask before a search link types text; keep a note link's text with its request

- search?fallbackText= from outside now asks first, like every other link
  that carries input. Always Allow keys it as the row `search`.
- A create-note link's text travels with its request. A second link's text
  can no longer end up in the next note made with Cmd-N.
- allowedDeepLinks replaces deepLinkAllowedEntryIDs. The list holds a row
  plus its exact input, not entry IDs.
- DeepLinkInput's initializer defaults each part to nil.
- Removes comments that only restated the code.

* Refuse bad link input before asking; show batch links; pass extension context

- set-volume with a level outside 0-100, and note/. or note/.., report the
  link before any question.
- The question for a list of quicklinks shows each name and its link.
- Extension links read context (or launchContext) as one JSON object and
  hand it to the command as props.launchContext.

---------

Co-authored-by: Rohith Gilla <gillarohith1@gmail.com>

pending.subject: Support AES-GCM in the extension crypto shim (#1767)
pending.body:
Several extensions (2FAS, Aegis, Proton Authenticator and others) seal
their vaults with aes-256-gcm. The shim accepted only CBC and ECB, so
createCipheriv threw ERR_CRYPTO_UNKNOWN_CIPHER.

The host gains gcmSeal and gcmOpen on CryptoKit. gcmOpen returns null
when the tag does not verify, and the runtime throws Node's own error
for it, with no code. Nonces of 12 bytes or more and 16-byte tags work;
other tag lengths throw instead of producing a wrong tag.

pending.subject: Move fullscreen windows between displays and add display-move options (#1785)
pending.body:
* Keep the window gap constant across display moves

Next/Previous Display scaled a non-tile window against visibleFrame, so a
maximized window's gap grew or shrank with the display. Measure against each
display's canvas after its own gap instead.

* Move fullscreen windows between displays and add display-move options

A geometry command on a natively fullscreen window now exits fullscreen,
waits for it to leave, and places the window. Next and Previous Display
re-enter fullscreen on the destination. A newer command on the same window
cancels a running transition. A fullscreen write that times out is no
longer followed by a green-button press that could flip the window back.

Adds Wrap around displays and Keep aspect ratio, both on by default.

* Wait out the fullscreen exit and restore back into fullscreen

Leaving fullscreen now waits a fixed 750 ms for the system animation before
placing, since AXFullScreen flips as the animation starts and some apps undo
a frame written before it ends. Only a failed AXFullScreen write is confirmed
by polling, and an unanswered read counts as not yet rather than as out of
fullscreen. A failed write never falls through to the green button.

A command that takes a window out of fullscreen makes fullscreen its restore
point, so Restore re-enters it, and does nothing after a fullscreen display
move. Restore after Tinycast's own Toggle Fullscreen still returns the
original frame.

* Drop comments that restate the code and reflow a docs paragraph

pending.subject: Sign releases with Developer ID and notarize them (#1803)
pending.body: Release jobs read the Developer ID identity and an App Store Connect API key from the release environment, sign with a secure timestamp, notarize the DMG once, and staple both the DMG and the app the updater's zip carries. The updater drops its self-signed leaf fallback, which no Developer ID build can use. Local builds keep Tinycast Self-Signed.

pending.subject: Trust updates through a release key or the running identity, and install them at quit (#1808)
pending.body:
* Trust updates through a release key or the running identity, and install them at quit

The updater trusted a downloaded bundle only through a pinned team ID, so a pin that was wrong or changed stranded every copy. It now accepts a sealed bundle when either its zip carries an Ed25519 signature from Tinycast's release key, or it satisfies the running copy's own designated requirement, so either root can change without stranding anyone. CI signs each updater zip and refuses to publish when the built app trusts a different key. A verified update now stays staged and is swapped in at quit, so the old process never loads resources or helpers from the new bundle.

* Report an unwritable install location before downloading an update

The swap now runs at quit, too late to show an error, so the updater checks up front that it can replace its own bundle.

* Delete CompactFavoritesMigration, shipped in 0.12.8

A migration lives for one stable release; 0.12.8 shipped it, so check-migrations failed lint and would have stopped the next Release run.

* Drop comments that restated the code

* Validate update seals strictly and discard a refused staging copy

kSecCSStrictValidate also rejects unsealed extra content and malformed resource envelopes; a verify that fails no longer leaves the expanded bundle in Caches.

* Check the staged update's seal again before the swap

Caches can be trimmed between staging and quit; a copy that no longer validates is discarded instead of installed. The strict check takes about 50 ms on the shipped bundle.

* Install only the verified update, and gate releases on the last one

The staged copy waits in Caches until quit, where any process can rewrite it, so the swap now
re-runs the trust check and requires the code-directory hash recorded at verification. It also
skips the swap when the installed app is no longer the version running, so a brew upgrade made
meanwhile is never rolled back.

- The release-key path still requires a Developer ID signature from any team, so a leaked key
  alone cannot ship an ad-hoc build.
- check-update-path.sh fails a release unless the last one on its channel trusts the new key or
  is satisfied by the new signature, which turns "never change both" into a gate.
- A .sig that fails to download is logged, and a cancel during it stops the update at once.
- A launch of an older version than the one staged reports that the update was not installed.
- signing.md takes the password and release key at gh's prompt, out of shell history.

* Drop the Developer ID switch notes about self-signed copies

Only the rules still true for every build stay: Developer ID lives in CI alone, and how TCC grants follow a renewal or a new team.

* Show a staged update from Check for Updates instead of offering it again

Offering it again downloaded the same release once more, and a cancel then lost the staged copy the next quit would have installed.

* Stop bumping stable in the tap now that it is in homebrew/cask

* Fix the update-path check's requirement syntax, and log update failures readably

`codesign -R="=…"` passed `==…`, a requirement syntax error, so the first release without a release
key in its predecessor would have failed the check. Update failures now log their detail publicly
instead of as <private>, and the signature decodes without a lossy String conversion.

pending.subject: Replace the update window with a pill in the palette (#1817)
pending.body:
* Replace the update window with a pill in the palette

An update now shows as a tinted pill in the palette footer, or at the end
of the search capsule in compact mode. The download, verification, staging
and swap at quit do not change. The app no longer shows release notes, and
the Changelog menu item opens tinycast.dev/changelog.

* Let a manual update check run during an automatic one

A manual check that met an automatic one in flight returned false, so it
reported that GitHub was unreachable. It now makes its own request.

Also drops two update comments that no longer described the code.

* Make Later hide the update pill until the next launch

The × on an offered version saved it as skipped, so its pill never came
back and a user could stay on an old version until the next release. It
now records nothing. The pill returns at the next launch, or sooner for a
newer release. The skip record is gone, and old cache files still decode.

* Add natural-language dates, zoned times, compound rates and split bills to the calculator

Dates: ordinals and day.month (days until 29th of october), in N days,

* Fix calculator review findings on overnight spans, spaced meridiems and New Year phrases

An overnight span now advances its end in the source zone, so a DST change
between the two ends no longer shifts it by an hour. A spaced am/pm joins a
clock that carries minutes. Fixed-date occasions recur when a clock time on
them has passed, and New Year phrases count as moments in arithmetic.

A split divides the unrounded amount before any target, so $1 / 6 split 2 matches $1 / 6 / 2 and a timespan is shared whole. pending.subject: Calculator: unit fractions, rounding, interest, date spans and more phrases (#1823)
pending.body:
* Calculator: unit fractions, rounding, interest, date spans and more phrases

- A tight fraction before a unit is one amount (`5/16" in mm`, `1 1/2 cups`),
  and `"`/`'` after a number are inches and feet; spaced `/` still divides.
- Spoken `squared`, `cubed`, `to the power of`, `root n of`, `log x base b`,
  `half of`, and `$2M` / `€1.5bn` after a currency.
- Percent phrases keep money and units (`25% off $60`) and add `on`,
  `as a % of`, `off/on what`, `what % off/on`, `a to b is what %`, `as %`.
- New CalcRounding: `to 2 dp`, `rounded up/down`, `to nearest hundred`,
  `as fraction`. New CalcFinance: compound interest and loan payments.
- Date spans (`may 1 to may 31`, `days between …`, `10pm to 2am`,
  `through`, `in workdays`), `after`/`before`, `weekday on`, `days in`,
  `current timestamp` and bare epoch `to date`.
- `in hours and minutes` timespans, `as` as a conversion connector, unit
  aliases (`nautical miles`, `ly`, `sq ft`, `°`), and a rate times time now
  answers in the rate's numerator (`60 mph * 2.5 hours` is `150 mi`).

Closes #1706

* Calculator: questions in words, spoken math, statistics, holidays and units

- Questions in words: a leading `what is` / `calculate`, a trailing `?`,
  `convert 5 km into miles`, `how many feet in a mile`, `cm in 5 inches`,
  `exchange rate for usd to eur`.
- New CalcSpokenMath: `is 97 prime`, `clamp`, `remainder of`, proportions,
  `5 choose 3`, permutations, logarithm phrases, `5 root of 32`,
  multipliers.
- New CalcStatistics: `median`, `count` and `standard deviation of`, with
  lists lowered to the function call so units are kept.
- Percent: classic orders, `% change from`, `4 out of 10`, rule of three,
  comment words, and tax/VAT/GST on, of and in a price.
- Rounding `up`/`down`/`to next`/`to last` and fraction steps; number forms
  `to sci`, `to dms`, `to hms`, `to laptime`, `to multiplier`, `to base 7`.
- New CalcMixedUnits: `to feet and inches`, `to lb oz`,
  `to years and months` for any two units of one kind.
- New CalcRatePhrases and CalcGrowth: `$50/hr for 3 hours`, downloads,
  playback speed, rates per unit, growth, decay and time to reach a value.
  CalcFinance adds present value, returns, loan interest and the
  investment a yield needs.
- Dates: `days left in 2026`, `workdays in march`, week and day of month,
  `whole`, `halfway between`, `previous`/`midday`/`p.m.`, `to iso`.
- New CalcHolidays: Easter, Orthodox Easter, Chinese New Year, Ramadan,
  Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha and Hanukkah from computus and Foundation's
  calendars; moon-sighted days show `(±1 day)` on the card.
- Zones: `date in tokyo`, `local time in tokyo`, `diff london & tokyo`,
  `time in tokyo when it's 5pm in london`.
- Units: capacitance, inductance, conductance, magnetic flux and flux
  density, torque and moles, plus parsecs, carats, troy ounces, barrels

now passes clicks through rather than starting a drag, and the panel
claims a double-click on the band before AppKit's own title-bar
action can run, to keep "double-click moves Notes to the top right"
working.

pending.subject: Reasoning effort picker for the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs (#1830)
pending.body:
* Reasoning effort picker for the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs

Every connection but OpenRouter now takes per-model declared levels from
the ladder its destination defines. Anthropic's catalog pre-ticks them
from capabilities.effort. A picked level goes out as Responses'
reasoning.effort, Chat Completions' reasoning_effort or Anthropic's
output_config.effort; Default sends nothing.

Closes #1826.

* Use each Claude model's own output ceiling and adopt catalog levels

Anthropic's /v1/models states each model's max_tokens; store it per model
and send it, falling back to 32,000 for a model whose ceiling was never
read. Opening the connection editor fills levels and limits for models
saved before the catalog was read, so nothing needs re-adding.

* Remove comments that restate the code

pending.subject: Add chat presets: start an AI Chat from saved instructions, model and tools (#1796)
pending.body:
* Add chat presets: start an AI Chat from saved instructions, model and tools

A preset is a name, icon, instructions, optional model and MCP server set,
edited in Settings > AI > Chat Presets. Each preset is a launcher row with
its own alias and shortcut, and an empty AI Chat can pick one from the
composer. The chat stores a copy of the preset, so later edits never
change what an older chat sends.

Closes #1794

* Remove the onboarding UI harness

It opened real windows on screen during every test run. It was the only
harness using the exclusive queue, so that marker goes too.

* Pick chat presets only from the AI Chat composer

Presets leave the launcher: no launcher row, alias, shortcut or deep
link. The composer's preset menu shows on every empty chat and offers
Add Chat Preset… when none exist. Settings rows get a trash button with
a confirmation dialog, the editor uses generic placeholders, and its
buttons fill the row.

* Keep Settings editors on screen

An editor centred on a Settings window dragged into a corner opened with
its buttons off screen, and the dim over the window left no way out. The
editor now stays inside the screen's visible frame and is laid out again
whenever the Settings window moves.

* Follow preset edits in empty chats and keep presets off device

An empty chat now follows edits to its preset and drops a deleted one,
so the first send carries the preset as it stands. A preset chat reopens
on the tools it last sent with, ⌘N in an empty chat clears its preset,
and the window's open policy keeps an empty chat that has one.

Apple Intelligence gets no preset: no instructions on device, no preset
menu on that route, and no on-device model in the preset editor.

Presets load only while AI is on. The Settings views reach
AIChatCoordinator through the environment, and the dialog rule now
allows SwiftUI's sheet dialogs in the Settings window, as five panes
already use them.

Let the palette's Liquid Glass own its rounded corner (#1835)
pending.body:
The expanded palette drew a rectangular NSGlassEffectView behind its
SwiftUI content and cut it round with the root clip, so the glass rim
stopped at each corner. The palette now applies SwiftUI's own
glassEffect in the panel's rounded shape (identity while compact), so
the rim follows the curve. AppKit owns only the window.

The root clip stays: it is what lets macOS read the panel's outline for
the system shadow. ui.md now says so, and why bare glass as a
borderless window's content makes macOS shadow the default window
outline instead.

pending.subject: Install from homebrew/cask; the tap keeps only the universal build (#1836)
pending.body:
tinycast and tinycast@beta are in homebrew/cask, and the tap carries only
tinycast-universal. The README, website and release notes install with a plain
brew install --cask, with no tap or brew trust line, and point Intel Macs to the
tap. release.yml no longer bumps a cask from the build job: only the universal
job writes to the tap. The Discord announcement drops the tap path.

pending.subject: Clip the ⌘K menu in SwiftUI and restore the panel scrim (#1839)
pending.body:
* Clip the ⌘K menu to its glass in SwiftUI

MenuPanel cut its hosted menu round with a CAShapeLayer mask, built from a
clip path every menu had to supply. The menus now clip themselves to the
shape their glass already uses (PopoverMenu, the extension Actions panel
and the extension picker list), and the menu window's system shadow traces
that outline, as it does the palette's root clip.

MenuPanelClipPath, the three clip closures and the mask set-up are gone,
along with the hosting-layer settings that only served the mask.

* Restore the panel scrim, with the glass behind it

Reverses #1748's scrim removal: panelScrim is back on the palette, the compact
bar, dialogs, HUDs, Notes, Camera, quick-action results and settings editors.

The palette, dialogs and settings editors now draw their glass behind the scrim
instead of passing the scrim to it as content, so the scrim also dims the rim.
That matches the thinner top and bottom rim of a glass-behind surface (84 against
107 on a dark desktop). Content above the scrim no longer gets the glass's
legibility boost: Dark title text peaks at 229 instead of 255.

The compact bar masks the scrim to its animated capsule and buttons, and leaves
the selected button out so its tint stays undimmed.

* Drop comments that restate the scrim and clip code

pending.subject: Restore Form fields that set storeValue (#1841)
pending.body:
Action.SubmitForm now saves every field that sets storeValue, as JSON, to
ExtensionStorage.formValues, keyed by command and field id. The launch
context hands the running command's saved values to the runtime, and an
uncontrolled field with storeValue starts from its saved value on its first
render, so React's form state and the native control agree. A DatePicker
decodes its saved ISO string back to a Date. A controlled value always wins,
and nothing is saved until the form is submitted.

pending.subject: Serve exchange rates from tinycast.dev (#1842)
pending.body:
The calculator fetched fiat and crypto rates from Raycast's private backend.
The website Worker now serves both at /api/v1/currencies and
/api/v1/currencies/crypto, in the same response shape, built from the CC0
fawazahmed0/exchange-api daily USD snapshot and kept in the edge cache.

pending.subject: Lay out bilingual dictionary entries (#1843)
pending.body:
* Lay out bilingual dictionary entries

Oxford bilingual dictionaries (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, German, …) use a span schema DictionaryMarkup did not know, so a whole entry rendered as one paragraph. Map hwg, gramb, semb, exg and the idiom/phrasal-verb/compound sections onto the existing blocks, and restore the word breaks the stylesheet draws by margin.

* Lay out every Apple dictionary the way its stylesheet does

Group examples tight under their sense, read an example's bullet sn as a bullet, number thesaurus senses, break on x_xo1 and before Duden's colonless examples, and drop a separator that leads a block. Checked against all 78 dictionaries in Apple's catalog.

* Choose between dictionary and thesaurus in the header

Dictionary stays the default and the lookup it always was; Thesaurus asks only the enabled thesauri, through the header button or ⌘P. Read the plain Dictionary Development Kit template too, whose h1/p records were dropped.

pending.subject: Sharpen the palette corner and reopen compact after a restore (#1844)
pending.body:
* Cut the palette's corner with the clip alone

The expanded palette drew its glass in the panel's rounded shape and then
clipped the root to the same curve. SwiftUI glass feathers its own edge, so
the corner was anti-aliased twice and read soft: an alpha ramp of 3-8 px at
the curve, and a corner eroded by about 2 px.

The glass is now square, and the root clip alone cuts the corner, as before
#1835. The corner matches a single clip pixel for pixel, the rim still lights
the curve, and over a white desktop the system shadow and hairline follow
all four corners with no pale rectangle. ui.md now says to keep the glass
square, and why.

* Summon the compact bar again after an expanded restore

In compact mode, ↓ and an Escape that clears the query both set
forceExpanded, and only the launcher's prepare cleared it. Pop to Root
Search keeps the screen for its timeout, so every summon inside that window
reopened the full panel with an empty field, and compact seemed to stop
working until the timer ran out.

A summon of a hidden palette now clears forceExpanded whenever the field is
empty, before the window is sized and ordered front. A kept query, screen or
extension still restores expanded.

pending.subject: Draw the compact bar on the expanded panel's glass (#1845)
pending.body:
The compact bar's own small glass shapes rendered the thin, clear control
material, so it never matched the expanded panel's frost. Compact now keeps
the expanded window height and clips the panel's own glass and scrim to the
bar, animating the clip with the reveal's springs.

This reverts commit 7f3e5b45598d359fde23452fe009513aae6fcdbc.
